title: Black Panther Political Prisoners — Roster
description: Consolidated roster of 27 Black Panther Party political prisoners, giving for each a capture date, age at capture, sentence, years served and an estimated cost of incarceration. Twenty-two are listed as imprisoned; five appear under the heading Joined the ancestors while in custody. Header quotes Che Guevara and totals the group time in captivity at over 800 years. PDF metadata dates the file to May 2013; the content is contemporaneous with the December 2012 companion sheet.

title: Over 800 Years in Captivity
description: December 2012 broadside arguing that the United States holds political prisoners while officially denying it, and counting more than 69 people then imprisoned in the US for political actions or beliefs, twenty of them former Black Panther Party members. Companion piece to the 27-name roster.

title: Hugo Pinell
description: Case and biographical material on Hugo Yogi Pinell of the San Quentin Six, one of the longest-held prisoners in California at the time of publication. Image-only scan with no extractable text layer.

title: Geronimo ji Jaga (Pratt)
description: Seven-page file on Geronimo ji Jaga Pratt, the Los Angeles Black Panther leader imprisoned for 27 years before his conviction was vacated. Image-only scan with no extractable text layer.

title: Marilyn Buck
description: Profile of Marilyn Buck, described in the source material as one of the longest-held political prisoners in the United States, covering her convictions and the conspiracy case arising from the escape of Assata Shakur. Scanned newsprint; the text layer is present but heavily degraded.

title: A Long Time Political Prisoner Requests Your Assistance — Bashir Hameed
description: Support appeal summarising the treatment of Bashir Hameed at Sullivan Correctional Facility, quoting from his own letter about chest pains, a work reassignment from the yard crew to the gymnasium, and the administrative treatment that followed. Useful for his health and custody history, which the roster sheets do not carry.

title: Herman Wallace: The Triumph of Pantherism
description: Statement from Herman Wallace of the Angola 3, written from his sickbed and thanking supporters, with the line that the state may have stolen his life but his spirit continues to struggle alongside Albert Woodfox. He refers to the oath he took in 1970. PDF metadata dates the file to September 2013, two weeks before his release and death.

title: Angola 3 Poster
description: Single-sheet campaign poster for the Angola 3 — Albert Woodfox, Herman Wallace and Robert King. Image-only scan with no extractable text layer.

title: New Trial Sought for Herman Wallace
description: Newspaper report by Anne Pruder on a 19 September hearing held in a courtroom inside Angola, at which Wallace counsel argued for a new trial on the ground that the prosecution had withheld evidence that would have won an acquittal. Names the Angola 3 as Wallace, Albert Woodfox and Robert King Wilkerson.

title: The Angolite, 1995
description: Twelve pages from the prisoner-produced magazine of the Louisiana State Penitentiary, carrying material on Herman Wallace and Albert Woodfox. Image-only scan with no extractable text layer.

title: The Angolite, 1995 — second file
description: A second eleven-page scan from the same 1995 Angolite material. Held separately rather than merged because the two files are not identical and the overlap has not been checked page by page. Image-only scan with no extractable text layer.

title: Marshall Law: Marshall Eddie Conway Event
description: Event flyer opening on the framing of Eddie Conway in 1970 for the murder of a Baltimore police officer at the age of 24, and the forty years he had then served. PDF metadata dates the file to March 2011, three years before his release.

title: San Francisco 8 — Black August 2009
description: Black August 2009 material on the San Francisco 8 prosecution, dated by PDF metadata to 1 August 2009, weeks after charges were dropped against four defendants and Jalil Muntaqim entered a no-contest plea.

title: Henry ShaSha Brown Memorial and Political Prisoner Fundraiser
description: Flyer and organising minutes for a 28 January 2005 event at St Mary Church on West 126th Street, Harlem, celebrating the life of Henry ShaSha Brown. Listed speakers include the attorney Gerald Lefcourt and the former political prisoners Shujaa Graham and Herman Ferguson — names worth following up as separate cases.

title: Attica to Abu Ghraib: An Organizing Conference on Human Rights, Torture and Resistance
description: Programme for a two-day organising conference on 22 and 23 April, sponsored by the International Human Rights Initiative, opening with Congresswoman Cynthia McKinney. The document carries no year; the description of McKinney as recently returned to office points to 2005, when she retook her seat, but that is an inference and the year is left unset.

title: International Day of Solidarity with Political Prisoners, December 3, 2005
description: Twenty-eight page programme for the 3 December 2005 International Day of Solidarity with Political Prisoners, collecting statements written by political prisoners held in the United States. The longest document in this set and the one most likely to name people not yet in the database.

title: Sekou Odinga Defense Committee
description: Material from the Sekou Odinga Defense Committee on his capture, prosecution and treatment in custody. Image-only scan with no extractable text layer; the December 2012 date in the PDF metadata records when the file was made, not the document, which belongs to the 1980s campaign.
